clue.text: Without prior help, unruly characters in form drop out

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, of the word form are made unruly, so they are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw from a race or contest, to drop out

explanation.surface: Some unruly people drop out of a school form, with nobody having helped them beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly characters in' turns FORM into FROM. 'drop out' is a verb: to scratch is to withdraw an entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting from scratch means beginning from nothing, with no earlier work or assistance to build on.

clue.text: Assembly of relatively 9 10

parts.note: 9 10 is LIMITED COMPANY, so the clue reads as company limited to relatives, an assembly of kin

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 9 and 10 gives 'relatively limited company': a get-together restricted to relations, with 'relatively' punning on relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion of relations is company restricted to kin, a business-sounding phrase recast as a domestic party.

clue.text: Leading spinner playing first

indicators.note: first says the word for playing comes before the spinner in the answer

parts.note: a performer who is playing is on, on stage
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A spin bowler leads the attack by bowling first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler, the surface reading; here it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front, ahead of the field or in charge, is being in the top position.

clue.text: More bubbly fluid residues English once disposed of

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters left over are free to flow into a new order
once disposed of says the English letter is removed a single time, so only one of the two goes

explanation.surface: Leftover fluid residues get thrown away, leaving something frothier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once disposed of' removes a single E from RESIDUES, leaving RSIDUES, which 'fluid' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapy liquid has suds on it, so a frothier one has more of that foam.

clue.text: Delivered cold-weather spray to keep temperature rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
to keep means the spray holds the temperature letter within it

parts.note: a de-icer is sprayed on windscreens in frosty weather

explanation.surface: A winter spray was supplied that holds the temperature steady as it climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts T inside DEICER, giving DETICER; 'rising' reads that upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech or poem that was delivered was spoken aloud before an audience, i.e. recited.

clue.text: Indestructible clue is appearing regularly in paper

indicators.note: in says the picked letters sit inside the newspaper name

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper

indicators.note: appearing regularly picks every second letter of the words clue is

explanation.surface: A crossword clue that is published regularly in a newspaper seems to last for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes L, E, S from 'clue is'. The Times is a London daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never ages or wears out is unaffected by time, a loose synonym for indestructible.

clue.text: Lead singer's notes?

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal, so notes sung by lead would be music of that metal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead singer' looks like the band's frontman; read Lead as the element, a heavy metal, and its notes are a rock genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud rock style is named after dense elements such as lead, so a lead singer's notes are that genre.

clue.text: Spotted learner driver taken into police custody

indicators.note: taken into says the learner letter goes inside the policeman word
custody reinforces that the police word holds the learner within it

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver, caught out, is taken into police custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen' but means covered in blobs. A bobby is a British policeman; L is the learner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in blotches or dots, a surface is splodgy, the sense the adjective carries.

clue.text: What Daisy and friend did presumably in series 4?

definitions.text: What Daisy and friend did presumably
definitions.meaning: in the song Daisy Bell the pair ride a bicycle built for two
4 is RECITED, so this means performed as a sequence, delivered in rotation

explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Bell is the old music-hall song about a bicycle made for two. The cross-reference to 4 gives 'in series recited'.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a bicycle is pedalling, and going round in a repeating series is turning through a loop; one verb covers both.

clue.text: Business conducted outside one US college by theatre cast

indicators.note: outside says the word for conducted sits around the other pieces

parts.note: an orchestra conducted is led
I is the Roman numeral one
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
a theatre company is the troupe of actors

explanation.surface: A firm is run from outside a single American college by a troupe of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm whose owners have restricted liability is a standard kind of commercial enterprise.

clue.text: See 9
Writer needing reason to join dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
the point of something is its reason or purpose

explanation.surface: An author needs a reason to go along to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author; it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is an instrument that writes, so it is a writer in the crossword sense of thing that writes.

clue.text: Constant contributor to employ alumni

indicators.note: contributor to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A faithful donor gives to a fund for hiring former students.
explanation.definitionFit: A constant friend is steadfast and faithful, the same quality as unwavering allegiance.

clue.text: Eastern regime brought back torture, any number fleeing

indicators.note: brought back says the remaining letters are read in reverse
fleeing says the number letter departs from the word for torture

parts.note: agony is torment, torture
N is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: An oriental regime revived torture, and crowds ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeing' takes N out of AGONY, leaving AGOY; 'brought back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian discipline of posture and breathing is a regimen originating in the East.

clue.text: New union member's boss booked family accommodation

parts.note: a bride is a new member of a marriage, a union; with the 's she becomes brides
a head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: The newly-wed's employer reserved rooms for her relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' looks like reserved; it means found in a book: Brideshead is the Flyte family seat in Evelyn Waugh's novel Brideshead Revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: The stately house in Waugh's novel is the Flyte family's home, accommodation that exists in a book.

clue.text: Wrongdoing concealed by angry criminal where lawyers abound

indicators.note: concealed by says the wrongdoing is hidden within the scrambled letters
criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of angry are rearranged

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A crime is covered up by an angry crook in a place full of lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' puts SIN inside GRAYN, which 'criminal' makes from the letters of the angry word. Gray's Inn is one of London's four Inns of Court, where barristers belong.
explanation.definitionFit: This London Inn of Court houses barristers' chambers, so legal professionals are plentiful there.

clue.text: Organised peace tours where atmosphere's lacking

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Package tours for peace have been laid on, but they lack any buzz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atmosphere' reads as ambience, but it is the literal air of a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond a planet's envelope of air lies the void of the cosmos, with no air at all.

clue.text: Distant Piscean?

definitions.meaning: distant means aloof, standoffish in manner
Piscean read literally means belonging to fish, the sign Pisces being the fishes

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, OF FISH is what Piscean means; the question mark flags that wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distant is cool and aloof; the second reading splits it to describe the sign of the fishes.

clue.text: Carriage parking originally halved at public school

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of each of the three words parking, halved, at

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public, i.e. private fee-paying, school

explanation.surface: A school's car park was cut in half to make room for carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' reaches across three words, not just 'parking'. Eton College is an elite English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light open four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Elegant six-footer that aids Sizewell operation

parts.note: cool means stylish, elegant
an ant is an insect, with six legs or feet

explanation.surface: A smart tall person helps run Sizewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is a six-legged insect. Sizewell is a nuclear power station in Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor needs fluid circulating to carry away heat, so this substance keeps the plant running.

clue.text: Tree from China, source of myrrh

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a pal

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter of myrrh

explanation.surface: A tree from China yields myrrh.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so 'china' means pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The date and coconut are examples of this tropical tree with fan-shaped fronds.

clue.text: Scrooge catching Cratchitt's latest name for him

indicators.note: catching says the miser word holds the picked letter inside it

parts.note: Scrooge, from Dickens, stands for any miser

indicators.note: latest takes the final letter of Cratchitt

explanation.surface: Scrooge catches what his clerk Bob Cratchit last called him.
explanation.definitionFit: A man is addressed by this title, the full form of Mr, so it is a way of naming him.

clue.text: Hot-headed knight getting out of his glad rags

indicators.note: getting out of says the knight letter leaves the word for glad rags

parts.note: finery is one's best clothes, glad rags
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A quick-tempered knight undresses from his best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery person is quick to anger, flaring up, which is what hot-headed describes.

clue.text: Contentious weapons in a vault, with others unopened

parts.note: a burial vault is a tomb

indicators.note: unopened says the other vaults lose their opening letter

parts.note: others means further vaults, so more tombs

explanation.surface: Disputed weapons are hidden in a vault, the rest sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with others' means the vault plus other vaults: TOMBS, which 'unopened' shortens to OMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear arms are highly controversial weapons, provoking protest and argument for decades.

clue.text: Mac, small one I found in store

indicators.note: found in says the letter I sits within the store word

parts.note: a barn is a farm building used for storage

explanation.surface: A Scotsman found a little thing of mine in the store.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac stands for a Scot; the definition is a Scotsman's little one.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots use this word for a child, so a Scotsman's little one is his child.

clue.text: Parody about Liberal providing winter sports facility

indicators.note: about says the parody word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a skit is a short comic parody
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: A satire on the Liberals offers winter holiday amenities.
explanation.definitionFit: This cable apparatus carries skiers uphill, standard equipment at a winter resort.

clue.text: Adult paper under discussion

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
tissue is thin paper

explanation.surface: A grown-up's paper is being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter being debated is the point in question, the subject in dispute.

clue.text: Jar containing dipso's first drink

indicators.note: to jar is to jolt, so the letters are shaken into a new order
first picks the opening letter of dipso

explanation.surface: A jug holding a drunk's first drink of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container, or slang for a drink, but it is the anagram signal on CONTAINING plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit topped up with quinine mixer is a classic long drink served with ice and lemon.
